title: One canvas scroll: the knot editor's 2D view scrolls, pans and zooms the way the graph view does
description:
Two 2D canvases answer the wheel differently. The knot editor's view (MainScene's editorCamera) gets Camera2D.onScroll(boolean up, delta): any wheel or trackpad delta zooms by ZOOM_SPEED * delta * ScaleFactor, only the vertical axis counts, and a trackpad's horizontal swipe does nothing. The graph view tool (DslGraphView) has its own onScroll(deltaX, deltaY): the wheel and a two-finger swipe pan along both axes through its scroll bars (SCROLL_PAN_PX_PER_UNIT), Shift turns the wheel sideways, and Ctrl+wheel (pinch) zooms by ZOOM_PER_SCROLL_UNIT^delta about the cursor. So the same gesture zooms in one canvas and pans in the other, and the pan and zoom code is written twice.

Move the graph view's canvas scroll onto Camera2D, the class both canvases already use: two-axis scroll pans, Shift turns it sideways, Ctrl or pinch zooms about the cursor. The editor's view and DslGraphView then both use it, and DslGraphView keeps only its scroll-bar range. Other Camera2D users (trade map, line and shader scenes, IrregularGridScene) get the same behaviour; check each one still makes sense.

Panes (terminal, info, code, menus) are UI-8's MenuScrollBox and are out of scope.
definition-of-done:
1. One scroll/pan/zoom implementation on Camera2D; DslGraphView's own onScroll pan and zoom code is gone.
2. In the knot editor, as in the graph view (user, 2026-10-20): a plain wheel or two-finger swipe pans on both axes (the wheel no longer zooms), Shift+wheel pans sideways, and Ctrl+wheel or pinch zooms about the cursor.
3. Scroll bars are an option of the shared canvas scroll, not always on: the graph view turns them on, and the knot editor has none (user, 2026-10-20).
4. Every other Camera2D scene is checked, and any that should keep a different rule is listed on the ticket with the reason.
5. A test drives scroll deltas at 1.25 display scale through the automation server and checks pan and zoom on both canvases.
6. Launch entries and screenshots.
testing-plan:
1. Live: wheel, Shift+wheel, Ctrl+wheel and trackpad swipe/pinch in the knot editor and in the graph view on a model scene; the same gesture does the same thing.
2. ixdar-cli scroll on each canvas, reading the camera's pan and scale from ui-state.
3. mvn test.
changes-made: Camera2D.wheelScrolled(deltaX, deltaY, x, y, mods) is the one canvas scroll: over the camera's main view the wheel/swipe pans SCROLL_PAN_PX_PER_UNIT (30 px) per unit on both axes, Shift turns a vertical-only scroll sideways, Ctrl (pinch) zooms by ZOOM_PER_SCROLL_UNIT^deltaY about the cursor. Constants moved from DslGraphView; Camera2D.usesWheel is now always true and wheelZooms is gone.

Scroll bars are an option: Camera2D.scrollLimited plus scrollLeft/Bottom/Right/Top (the scroll range, moved from DslGraphView.rangeLeft etc.) clamp a scroll pan to the range grown to hold the view. DslGraphView turns it on and keeps its bars and range bookkeeping; its own onScroll pan/zoom code is gone and it calls camera.wheelScrolled. The knot editor has no limit and no bars.

Root-cause fix found by the zoom test: Camera2D.calculateCameraTransform truncated PanX/PanY to whole pixels, so each zoom step moved the cursor's point by up to 1 px and a pinch's many steps walked it away; offsets are now unrounded.

Input path: CameraController.wheelScrolled carries both axes, the cursor (window px) and the modifier bitmask (new KeyGuy.modifiers()); MouseTrap keeps the horizontal delta for a wheel-using controller instead of PointerDispatcher dropping it. Camera3D and ThirdPersonCamera ignore the new arguments. MainScene, TradeScene and IrregularGridScene no longer subscribe their Camera2D as a PointerRegion for the wheel (regions are never unsubscribed, so a claiming camera region would have stolen the wheel in later scenes); the trap's controller path reaches only the active scene's camera.

Camera2D users checked: knot editor (MainScene) and graph view now share the behaviour; TradeScene map and IrregularGridScene get pan-on-wheel, Ctrl-zoom about the cursor (a map/grid, so trackpad-style pan is sensible; mouse-wheel users must now hold Ctrl to zoom). Line/dash/bezier/circle demo scenes and the shader code pane: their Scene.camera2D is a fixed overlay camera, never the trap controller, so no wheel reaches it before or after. Held zoom keys still zoom about the view centre through Camera2D.onScroll(boolean, delta).

Tests: unit.input.Camera2DScrollTest at 1.25 scale (1024 window, 1280 framebuffer, view offset 195 px like the editor): wheel through MouseTrap+PointerDispatcher pans both axes and keeps the zoom; Shift sideways; 20 Ctrl pinch steps keep the cursor's point within 0.01 px; a cursor below the view scrolls nothing; a limited scroll stops at its range. mvn test: 614 run, 0 failed.

Live (ixdar-cli hover/key press+release/scroll, orbit-get and mesh-dsl-graph): ixdar-canvas plain scroll panX +30 panY +60 scale unchanged, Shift panX +30 only, Ctrl 10x0.2 scale 0.9->1.19025 with the cursor's point fixed (441.11, 470.26); graph view (mesh-viewer, coons_cube) Ctrl zoom 0.9->1.8102 about the centre, plain and Shift scrolls moved the bars by 15/30 px as before, 40 rightward swipes stop at the range's right edge. Pinch itself is not delivered by GLFW on Linux, and the web build's ctrlKey wheel is not mapped to MOD_CONTROL; Ctrl+wheel stands in, as before.

Rework (user: scroll was still written twice): Camera2D now owns the whole scroll range. New fields scrollHome* (moved from DslGraphView.home*), scrollContentWidth/Height and scrollOffsetX/Y; methods resetScrollRange (range = home, then grown), updateScrollRange (grow the range to hold the view and measure content and offsets, moved from DslGraphView.updateScrollBars), scrollTo(offsetX, offsetY) (moved from DslGraphView.panToScrollBars) and pan(dx, dy) (a drag-pan step that resets a limited range; MainScene's drag goes through it too). wheelScrolled's limited pan now clamps the offsets to [0, content - view] and scrolls to them, and a Ctrl zoom resets the range itself.

DslGraphView keeps only its own parts: rebuild() sets camera.scrollHome* from the layout's padded frame and calls camera.resetScrollRange(); focus() frames a rectangle then calls camera.resetScrollRange(); updateScrollBars() lays its two MenuScrollBars along the window edges and copies the camera's content and offsets into them; a bar press or thumb drag calls camera.scrollTo(bar offsets); a graph drag calls camera.pan; onScroll forwards to camera.wheelScrolled. Its resetScrollRange and panToScrollBars and its own range-growing and Ctrl-reset code are gone. Graph.java reads home_frame and scroll_range from the camera.
Knot editor (user ruling): no scroll bars and no limit; MainScene's Camera2D has scrollLimited false, so wheelScrolled pans freely and never touches the range.

Re-verified: mvn test 615 run, 0 failed (Camera2DScrollTest gains a limited-range test: a zoom resets the range to home and view, 200 swipes stop at the range's edge without growing it, a drag past the edge grows it). Live, ixdar-canvas: plain +30/+60, Shift +30 sideways, 60 swipes moved panX by 9000 with no limit, Ctrl 10x0.2 to 1.19025 with the cursor's point fixed; no bars drawn in the main view. Graph view (mesh-viewer, coons_cube): Ctrl 5x0.5 to 1.2764 about the centre with the range reset to home, plain/Shift moved the bars 15/30 px, 40 swipes stopped at offset 535 = content - view, a thumb drag scrolled 535 -> 349, a pan-drag past the edge grew the range to the view (733.35).

Round 3 (user: one class for 2D canvas scrolling, DslGraphView must not know scroll internals): new ixdar.input.CanvasScroll, a CameraController driving a Camera2D. It owns the wheel (two-axis pan, Shift sideways, Ctrl/pinch zoom about the cursor), the drag-pan (unlimited, growing the range, as intended), the held movement and zoom keys, and with scrollBars on the home range, the scroll range with its growth, reset and clamp, and the two MenuScrollBars (placement on the main view's edges, press/drag/release on a bar, drawing). Constants SCROLL_PAN_PX_PER_UNIT, ZOOM_PER_SCROLL_UNIT and BAR_STEP_PX moved there.

Camera2D is a camera again: it no longer implements CameraController, and every scroll field and method (scroll range, home, offsets, drag state, wheelScrolled, updateScrollRange, scrollTo, resetScrollRange, pan, inMainView) is gone. One zoom: Camera2D.zoomAbout(factor, x, y) replaces scale(); Ctrl-wheel zooms about the cursor and the held zoom keys (Camera2D.onScroll) about the view centre through it. mainViewBounds is now a public field for the scroller. The PanX/PanY rounding fix stays.

One input path: the MouseTrap controller. MainScene, TradeScene and IrregularGridScene set mouse.controller = new CanvasScroll(camera, false); DslGraphView sets the scene's controller to its CanvasScroll(camera, true) on activate and back to the orbit on deactivate. Tool.onScroll and the dispatcher's tool-wheel branch are removed; DslGraphView's onPress/onDrag/onRelease are gone, and its click (focus a box, double-click empty to frame all) moved to Tool.onClick, the click path the editor tools use. CameraController gains pointerReleased(), which MouseTrap calls on every left release, so a press on a scroll bar is no click on the canvas. KeyGuy.modifiers() inlined into MouseTrap.

DslGraphView now holds only graph things: it builds the layout, hands the scroller its home range (scroll.setHome with the padded layout bounds) on rebuild, asks it to frame a padded rectangle (scroll.frame) for focus, frame-all and hotspots, and calls scroll.drawBars() after drawing. Graph.java reads bars, home_frame and scroll_range from view.scroll.

Tests: unit.input.CanvasScrollTest (replaces Camera2DScrollTest) at 1.25 scale: wheel pans both axes via MouseTrap+PointerDispatcher, Shift sideways, 20 Ctrl steps keep the cursor's point within 0.01 px, outside the view nothing, with bars a zoom resets the range and swipes stop at it while a drag grows it, a press on a bar's arrow steps it and its release is no click. RingCameraDragHoverTest uses a CanvasScroll. mvn test 617 run, 0 failed.

Live, same gestures, same numbers in both canvases: ixdar-canvas plain +30/+60, Shift +30, Ctrl 10x0.2 to 1.19025 with the cursor's point fixed, drag 100 window px = 125 px, 60 swipes = -9000 px with no limit, no bars. Graph view: Ctrl 5x0.5 to 1.2764 about the centre, plain/Shift move the bars 15/30 px, 40 swipes stop at offset 535 = content - view, a thumb drag scrolls 535 -> 349, a pan-drag past the edge grows the range to 733.35, a click on a box focuses it, a double-click on empty space frames all, and after Ctrl+G off the wheel zooms the orbit again.

Round 4, input through the dispatcher: CanvasScroll is now also a PointerRegion, subscribed with its camera's main view bounds (MainScene views.get(VIEW_MAIN), TradeScene views.get(VIEW_MAIN), IrregularGridScene camera2D.mainViewBounds, DslGraphView the scene's pane on activate). The dispatcher hands it the wheel (claimsWheel while shown) and the presses on its scroll bars (claimsPointer only on a bar, then onPress/onDrag/onRelease), the MenuScrollBox pattern: one region per canvas that owns its bars, since MenuScrollBar.bounds is the box a bar runs along, not its strip. Presses on the view itself stay unclaimed, so tools and clicks keep the dispatcher's tool-then-trap route, and the drag-pan and held keys reach CanvasScroll as the trap's controller there.

PointerRegion.onScrollDelta now carries the cursor (framebuffer px) and the held modifier bitmask, which the dispatcher reads from the trap and its scene's key handler; MenuScrollBox, MenuBox and the test regions ignore them. CameraController.pointerReleased(), MouseTrap's controllerOwned check, and the wheelScrolled two-axis signature are removed: CameraController, Camera3D, ThirdPersonCamera and MouseTrap are back to master. CanvasScroll takes a shown supplier (the scene's or the graph's active flag), and DslGraphView unsubscribes its scroll on deactivate (PointerDispatcher.unsubscribe already existed; nothing called it).

Home range fix: CanvasScroll.setContent(left, bottom, right, top) takes the content bounds (DslGraphView hands over the padded layout frame) and resetRange makes the home range that rectangle grown about its centre to the main view's aspect ratio, which is exactly what frame-all shows. A wide, short graph no longer starts with a maxed vertical bar that stays maxed when zooming in. home_frame in mesh-dsl-graph now reports the content bounds.

Tests: CanvasScrollTest drives the wheel and bar presses through PointerDispatcher (region under the cursor, pressHolder on a bar, no claim below the view) and adds the wide-content test: 100 x 10 content at frame-all has both bars full; after a Ctrl zoom both thumbs are shorter than their tracks. mvn test 618 run, 0 failed.

Live: crawfish/IMG_4110 graph view (75 nodes, 22645 x 246 units): at start and after F both thumbs are 1220/1220 px; after Ctrl zoom 0.9 -> 1.19 both are 922/1220 (before the fix the vertical stayed full); plain/Shift moved the bars 15/30 px, 20 swipes stopped at offset 413 = content - view, a thumb drag scrolled 413 -> 240, a pan-drag past the edge grew the range to the view, a click on ring_34 focused it, F framed all, and after Ctrl+G off the wheel zooms the orbit again. Knot editor: plain +30/+60, Shift +30, Ctrl 10x0.2 to 1.19025 with the cursor's point fixed, drag 100 window px = 125 px, wheel over the terminal pane leaves the canvas alone, no bars.
review-summary: A new CanvasScroll, a pointer region the dispatcher routes to, owns all 2D canvas scrolling: wheel pan, Shift sideways, Ctrl zoom about the cursor, drag, keys, and optional scroll bars whose range is what frame-all shows. The knot editor and graph view scrolled differently because each had its own code.
